editorial.headline: Fertilisation Services With a Clear Bali Opening
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01612 covers contract-based farm fertilisation and related field services, open nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01612 is a practical field-service classification: fertilising agricultural land on a fee or contract basis. Its scope is not limited to applying fertiliser. The record also places seed or seedling planting, pest and disease control, and weed control inside the same activity when those services are performed for food crops, horticulture, or plantation crops under a service arrangement. In plain English, this is the code for an operator paid to carry out hands-on agricultural support work on someone’s land, rather than a code defined by the sale of an input or the ownership of the harvest.

That distinction matters because the code is built around service delivery. A business under this activity is registering the operational work of improving and protecting agricultural land and crops: fertilising, planting, and controlling pests, diseases, and plant competitors. The common thread is contract performance. The slim record does not create separate sub-rules for crop type beyond naming food crops, horticulture, and plantations, so the editorial reading should stay broad but disciplined: this is an agricultural support service for cultivated land, not a platform for inventing downstream trading, processing, or licensing consequences.

On scale, the record is unusually straightforward. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar business scales. That means the classification is not framed only for a large operator; it can also describe smaller service providers, provided the registered activity remains within the scope above. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100. In founder terms, the foreign-ownership ceiling in the record is 100%, so there is no partial foreign-share cap to explain here. The source stated for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

The Bali picture is also clear, and it is better than the cautionary pattern that often surrounds local PMA registration. The Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, permanently. But this activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that the OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore clean: for KBLI 01612, a foreign investor is looking at a nationally open activity with a 100% ceiling, and the Bali record does not block PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic.
